title: Marcus–Spielman–Srivastava partition theorem
statement:
Let $k\ge 2$ be an integer. Suppose $v_1,\ldots,v_m\in\mathbb{R}^d$ satisfy $\sum_{i=1}^m v_i v_i^*=I$, where $I$ is the identity matrix, and $\|v_i\|^2\le\varepsilon$ for all $1\le i\le m$. Then there is a partition $\{S_1,\ldots,S_k\}$ of $[m]$ such that
\[
\left\|\sum_{i\in S_j}v_i v_i^*\right\|\le \frac{(1+\sqrt{k\varepsilon})^2}{k},\qquad j\in[k],
\]
where $\|\cdot\|$ denotes the operator norm.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2015/17](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/13674), page 21. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.
